findings.reason: The duplication is real, and the source makes it plainer than the finding says. Checked at the pinned records and in both papers (globalmassey.pdf, SHA-256 d95100eb…, matching the red team's record; zceh.pdf, SHA-256 2e425ee6…, both fetched 2026-09-24 from www.math.univ-paris13.fr/~wittenberg/). PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/39 (construction, §3 p.8) and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81 (theorem, §5 p.18) carry the same name, both are missing, and both are routed part-ii to HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey under HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions (HW23 route 8, HW20 route 13). On p.8 HW23 only recalls the identification, as Hom(H^ab, k̄*) = Hom(H^ab, μ∞) ≅ Pic(V_k̄) as Γ_k-modules, citing '[HW20, §5]', and uses it for the exact sequence (3.1). HW20 §5.2 (p.18) proves it (Rosenlicht, Kummer theory, Pic(G_k̄) = 0). So HW23/39 is a cited input, and HW20's route reason, which says not to create another copy of the finite-stabilizer Picard interface, applies. Medium severity fits: without a recorded identification the design job for the shared candidate would plan the statement twice. The proposed fix needs one change. HW23/39 cannot simply be dropped from HW23's route: it is used in the paper (§3, (3.1)), so the extraction must keep it, and every missing item must be routed exactly once (§16). No 'coalescence' block for items exists in these records; the only such block in the repository, in PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22, identifies routes. The right fix follows the records' own practice for the supersolvable theorem, where PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/101 keeps its item with the note 'This is the same HW20 input already requested by PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23; the shared candidate owner below receives the proof once'. Keep HW23/39 on its route. Add to its note: 'This is [HW20, §5] = PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/81, cited, not proved, in this paper (§3 p.8). The shared candidate HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey builds it once, from HW20; this item is its consumer.' Add the matching sentence to HW20/81's note, naming HW23/39 as the consumer, and fold the μ∞ form into HW20/81's statement if wanted. Optionally, change HW23/39's kind to theorem, to match HW20/81.
